text: Large Language Models, or LLMs, are computer programs that can understand and generate human language. They work by predicting the next word in a sentence, based on patterns they learned from huge amounts of training data, such as books, websites and articles. Users communicate with LLMs through prompts, and good prompt engineering can greatly improve the results. These models are very useful for writing, translating and answering questions. However, they also have limits: they sometimes give wrong information, cannot access real-time data, and may reflect biases found in their training data. Therefore, it is important to check their answers carefully.
